name: ATLAS
summary: ATLAS is located at CERN LHC Point 1 near Meyrin. It is a general-purpose LHC detector, with dark matter forming part of its broad physics program.
detection_principle: Jets, leptons, photons and transverse-momentum imbalance reconstruct monojet, monophoton, invisible-Higgs and displaced-vertex signatures. Standard Model backgrounds from neutrinos and mismeasurement require separate control.

results.summary: The collaboration reports long-lived-dark-photon searches using displaced dilepton/photon vertices, interpreted as 95% confidence upper limits.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
